A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PaSa research. All 15 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on AutoScholarQuery and RealScholarQuery, Selector evaluation, component ablations and reward-coefficient sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a shared-subset comparison and action-cost sensitivity results in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Equation (3) changes the stated Crawler training target by moving the current-token KL penalty outside the discounted session sum. The Crawler/Selector architecture, actions and training stages remain unchanged. The PDFs establish a revision to the written procedure, without establishing an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same AutoScholarQuery and RealScholarQuery coverage and the same Selector evaluation task. The added 100-query comparison uses an existing AutoScholarQuery subset; no new dataset, domain or task scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: The retrieval and Selector comparator sets are unchanged, and v2's subset comparison uses the existing methods. The abstract's change from GPT-4 to GPT-4o corrects its naming to match the Google-with-GPT-4o baseline already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation of all methods on ChatGPT's existing 100-query subset and an action-cost sweep over 0, 0.1 and 0.2. Section 3.1 also changes the reported dataset-quality reviewers from one author to three, without establishing a rerun. Existing benchmark splits, model sizes and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G.2 adds an action-cost sensitivity study examining retrieval quality and excessive actions. The existing reward-coefficient sweep gains final precision and recall measurements in v2 Table 8. Component ablations and the decision-order comparison are retained; Figure 3's training curves are relocated unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals, variability across repeated runs, significance tests or random seeds. The new annotation consistency thresholds describe quality control, rather than uncertainty estimation for experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: Main benchmark, Selector and component-ablation scores remain identical. v2 adds subset results in Table 14, including recall 0.5328 for PaSa-7b and 0.4488 for PaSa-GPT-4o; action-cost results in Table 15; final precision/recall for the reward sweep; and RealScholarQuery answer-count statistics. These are additional results under their stated conditions, not performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The KL-term revision in Equation (3) is mathematically substantive: v1 repeatedly includes the fixed current-token penalty within the remaining-session sum, whereas v2 subtracts it once. The accompanying summation reindexing is equivalent. No new theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a two-agent paper-search system, two academic-search datasets, and strong real-world performance after synthetic-data training. The headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges untested scientific domains and the focus on 7B models, and explains action costs as preventing excessive unproductive searches. Section 5.2 newly interprets the PaSa-GPT-4o comparison as isolating RL's impact, although the compared systems also use different base models.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents dataset-quality criteria, annotation instructions and staged quality control, annotator payments, ensemble sampling decoding, and GPT-o1/PaSa-GPT-4o prompts. Existing PPO hyperparameters are retained and moved to Appendix D.2. These additions improve documentation without establishing corresponding changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning remain the same. The AGILE reference changes from its arXiv entry to its NeurIPS publication, including an updated title; this is the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and terminology corrections, expands explanations of sessions and evaluation, reorganizes appendix and prompt sections, and adds Limitations and Acknowledgments. The affiliation changes from ByteDance Research to ByteDance Seed. Most main-text prose and the section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds two result tables and two baseline-prompt tables, expands the reward-coefficient table, and moves the PPO hyperparameter table and Figure 3 into the appendix. Main result tables gain bold emphasis and a ChatGPT subset footnote. The basic layout and principal diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: The shared-subset comparison in Table 14 improves comparability with ChatGPT, while annotation guidance and previously missing baseline prompts improve reproducibility. The action-cost study and explicit limitations provide useful support and qualification around unchanged main results. The new claim that the GPT-4o comparison isolates RL is overstated because base models also differ, but this does not outweigh the limited gains in transparency and evaluation quality.
